LESSON: SIGN READING 10.2.1 INTENSIVE READING FACTUAL TEXTS OF ABOUT 400 WORDS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.2: Sign Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading Factual Texts of about 400 Words
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading Factual Texts of about 400 Words, part of Strand 10 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we sin read books? 2. Why should we make notes when sign reading? 3. What makes you a good reader?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading Factual Texts of about 400 Words together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn: Learning independently as learner, individually, skims and scans texts for information.

• Creativity and imagination: Making observations as learner discuss as they sign and relate ideas to their experiences.

• Digital literacy: Interacting with digital devices as learners watch a signed video or a video with closed captions on leisure time and write

the main points.

Values:
Responsibility: Determination as learners reads different texts and answer questions in pairs or small groups.

Link to other Subjects:

Learners are able to apply the skill intensive sign reading to their learning in Religious Education, Science and Technology, Agriculture, Social

studies and Creative arts.
